assign.request: UX rethink pass on /imagine/screens/ — five sentences, an actually-built alternative layout, measure and keep-or-revert, more visual, persistence check, ui-test, land.
steps: Build + measure alternative layout; keep or revert

log.msg: Five sentences (before), /imagine/screens/: what -- a landing page of eight small demo cards, each a tiny diagram of one way a click can reshape the screen. use -- click any of the eight cards, each opens a real page. goal -- leave knowing the two-word vocabulary (a click replaces the screen, or joins it and splits the space) across eight concrete examples. hard -- 2/5: round 1 already replaced the jargon paragraph with plain copy, but the eight diagrams are abstract outline rectangles with no numbers attached, so you cannot tell which demo actually proves something interesting until you click in and read its readme row. better -- put the number each demo actually measured on the card itself, and try a bigger layout to see if it helps legibility.

Alternative layout built and measured: the owner brief's 3-column card, rebuilt as one full-width row per demo (left title+intro, center the hop diagram handed more room, right the measured number). Content-extent height (the column's own, not documentElement.scrollHeight which is pinned to the viewport by the columns shell) went 695->1439px at 1280 and 856->1747px at 3440 -- roughly DOUBLED -- while width-used and dead-space were unchanged (46% / 1857px dead at 3440 both before and after), since this column is capped near 64em by the large width word regardless of what is inside it. Reverted: doubling scroll for zero width/dead-space gain fails the brief's own test (shorter without losing anything is better; this went the other way), and the pattern's real strength (a live demo, a metrics panel) does not fit here since every demo is one inert diagram and every readout is one sentence. Numbers and full writeup in doc/decisions.md. Kept the good half of the idea, shrunk to fit: each existing tile-wall card now also shows the number it measured, as a fourth short line (.screens-verdict).

Persistence check: grep -rn store()|localStorage public/imagine/screens/ found nothing. This realm persists none of its state -- every hop is a plain navigation (a url), never a saved value -- so no baseline() mark applies.

ui-test (drive.mjs) proved the primary gesture both directions, at 1280 and 3440: /imagine/screens/ -> click a card (Divide at 1280, Uneven at 3440) -> location.pathname becomes /imagine/screens/<slug>/ -> click the Screens crumb -> back to /imagine/screens/. Zero console errors on every one of the 8 recorded steps at each width (errors: [] throughout). Layout invariants checked directly: no real content at document x:0 belongs to this page (the x:0 boxes are the sites own left rail, unrelated to /imagine/screens/); every .md/.page-preview-desc/.screens-verdict block is capped exactly at its own computed max-width (var(--measure,40em), which resolves to 541px at 1280 and 648px at 3440 -- fluid, not a flat 640px -- and nothing exceeds it); zero framed boxes (border or box-shadow) touch the columns own left/right edge. All three pass.

Five sentences (after): what -- a landing page of eight demo cards, each a tiny diagram of one way a click can reshape the screen, now labeled with the actual number it measured. use -- click any of the eight cards, each opens a real page and shows the effect happening. goal -- leave knowing the two-word vocabulary (replace vs join) and which of the eight patterns fits a problem you actually have. hard -- 2/5, unchanged from before -- the intro was already plain and the diagrams are self-explanatory once you have clicked one, but the new number line answers does this actually hold up? without a click, which is a real (if modest) gain. better -- a hover/focus state on a cards diagram that animates the hop it represents in place would remove the last reason to click through blind just to see what a demo does.

assign.outcome: **Screens' index cards now carry the number each demo actually measured, and a 3-column-row alternative was built, measured, and reverted with real numbers.** Tried the owner's 3-column card as a full-width row per demo; it roughly doubled the column's own content height (695->1439px at 1280, 856->1747px at 3440) for identical width-used and dead-space (both stayed at 46% / 1857px at 3440, since the `large` width word caps this column regardless of what's inside it) — reverted, numbers in `doc/decisions.md`. Kept the useful half: each existing tile-wall card now shows a fourth short line, the demo's own measured stat (`.screens-verdict`), so a reader sees `1920/960/640/480 at 1920` etc. without clicking into the readme. Zero persistence in this realm. ui-test proved click-through and back at 1280 and 3440 with zero console errors; the three layout invariants pass.
